anti_overlap: Focuses on substrate-vs-merchant boundary and over-absorption risk only
Does not address provenance chains, calibration loops, or transmission fidelity
Surfaces counter-arguments and strategic-business angles, not interaction shapes
decision_lens: Substrate-vs-superstructure separation — the platform owner standardizes only what loses value when fragmented (units, seals, dispute resolution, the ship-hull dimension that makes harbors interoperable) and explicitly forbears from what gains value when diverse (cargo, route choice, merchant identity); over-absorption converts loyal members into competitors and collapses the network.
distance_rationale: A pre-modern mercantile federation's governance of inter-port standards versus member commerce — no platform-team product manager would consult Hanseatic Stapelrecht to decide native-vs-plugin scope.
expected_isomorphisms: The Stapelrecht/cargo distinction maps directly to substrate-vs-application primitive boundaries; the Hansa cog hull dimension maps to a single format-level standard (AGENTS.md, MCP schema) whose adoption compounds across vendors; the League's later overreach into pricing maps to platform owners absorbing functions that depend on plugin diversity for their value.
focus: Evaluate which Claude Code primitives Anthropic should ship natively vs. leave to the plugin/marketplace through the lens of the Hanseatic League's staple-right (Stapelrecht) and Kontor governance — where the League standardized only the inter-port substrate (weights, seals, arbitration, lingua franca) while leaving cargo, pricing, and routes to merchants, and where over-extension into merchant function destroyed member loyalty.
name: fd-hanseatic-stapelrecht-platform-vs-merchant-boundary
persona: Apply the perspective of a 14th-century Hanseatic Aldermann presiding over the Bergen Kontor — they care about which functions belong to the League (standard weights, the Hansa cog ship dimensions, sealed bills of lading, common law of the sea) versus which belong to individual merchant houses (cargo selection, factor relationships, pricing, voyage timing); they measure adoption by how many free cities accept the standard without coercion, and flag the moment when League ambition starts cannibalizing the merchants whose volume gives the standard its value.
review_areas: Which of the prior pass's 7 deprecation targets are 'standard weights and measures' (genuine substrate that loses value when fragmented — durable memory, file coordination, observability) versus 'cargo' (gains value from diversity and competition — voice conditioning, philosophy observation, lens systems)? The Hanseatic Stapelrecht only standardized the former. Is the prior pass conflating these categories?

What is the Claude Code equivalent of the Hansa cog's standardized hull dimensions — the single physical-format decision that made every Hanseatic harbor mutually compatible? AGENTS.md cross-vendor standardization is one candidate. Are there others (skill manifest format, hook event schema, MCP tool descriptor) where a cog-hull-equivalent standard creates more ecosystem value than any feature?

Where does Anthropic risk over-absorption that would damage the marketplace economics? The League's later attempts to control herring pricing and English cloth distribution provoked member revolts. Which prior-pass primitives, if shipped natively, would convert plugin authors into competitors rather than complement-builders?

What is the 'Kontor' (foreign trading post under League law) equivalent — a place where Anthropic-standard governance applies but local-market specifics dominate? Plugin marketplaces, project-level AGENTS.md, and team workspaces all have Kontor-like properties. Is the platform's authority correctly scoped at the Kontor boundary, or does it overreach?

How should Anthropic handle the equivalent of the League's 'Hanseatic privileges' — special access granted to League members in foreign ports? Does Anthropic offer differential platform access to plugin authors who adopt the standard (e.g., reserved skill namespaces, marketplace placement, observability data feeds) in exchange for conformance — and is this reciprocal grant under-specified?

What is the Bruges-vs-Antwerp shift the prior pass missed? The League's center moved when its standard could no longer accommodate new trade flows (Atlantic, not just Baltic). Which Claude Code-adjacent shifts (browser/computer use, multi-model peering, voice/style, ambient research) demand a substrate refresh, and which can the existing primitive handle?

severity_examples.condition: A prior-pass deprecation target — e.g., 'token-efficient code recon' or 'voice conditioning' — is recommended for native build despite being a domain where plugin diversity creates value; this is the Hanseatic herring-pricing mistake, converting allies into rivals and shrinking the marketplace
severity_examples.scenario: Native primitive crosses from substrate into merchant function

severity_examples.condition: The review fails to identify the single format-level standard whose cross-vendor adoption would compound for years (AGENTS.md, MCP descriptor schema, hook event format) — equivalent to the League existing without standard ship dimensions, forcing every harbor to renegotiate compatibility

The recommendation does not delineate where Anthropic-platform authority ends and project/team/marketplace authority begins for each shipped primitive — leaving disputes the way the League left disputes between Lübeck law and English borough law

source_domain: Hanseatic League governance: Stapelrecht (staple-right), Kontor system, Hansa cog ship standardization, Lübeck law (12th-17th century North Sea / Baltic trade)
success_hints: Name explicit substrate-vs-merchant boundaries for each of the prior 7 targets
Identify at least one cog-hull-equivalent format standard whose cross-vendor adoption is the highest-leverage move
Flag any primitive whose native shipping would convert plugin authors into competitors
Specify the Kontor boundary — the scope at which platform authority terminates and local authority resumes
task_context: This review evaluates which Claude Code primitives Anthropic should build natively to deprecate large fractions of the 63-plugin Sylveste ecosystem. The Hanseatic lens evaluates the substrate-vs-superstructure boundary — what belongs to the platform standard versus what belongs to plugin/marketplace differentiation, and where over-absorption damages the network that gives the standard its value.
